learning: No race data for this geometry yet. Expected effects to test: fewer line-loss events from the wider span, possible added oscillation from the 0.6 kg mass and 16 mm footprint, and whether base_speed 1.0 is too slow to complete within 3 s.
notes: Adopts the Builder's proposed seven-sensor 12 cm span, 16 mm footprint and 0.6 kg mass, with a moderate controller: kp 1.6, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.0 and last_direction line-loss recovery. Chosen to keep steering authority near the iteration 0 baseline while the geometry changes.
rationale: Iteration 0 gave no completions. Every run left the track with max_error of 0.060 to 0.064 m while rms_error stayed at 0.024 to 0.030 m, so the failures are short peak excursions on bends, not steady offset. The Builder's proposal widens sensing to seven sensors over 0.12 m with 16 mm footprints, and lowers mass to 0.6 kg. I keep that geometry unchanged so the controller is tested on the exact proposed platform. Sensor x runs from -0.06 (right) to +0.06 (left), so weights are negative on the right and positive on the left, matching the signal convention. Weights of -1.5 to +1.5 with kp 1.6 give an effective position gain of about 2.4 per unit of signal, close to the baseline's 2.5 on a ±1 scale. That keeps steering authority similar to iteration 0 while the wider span adds sensor coverage, so the controller is not made more aggressive at the same time as the geometry changes. kd rises to 0.5 to damp the faster turn response from the lighter 0.6 kg mass. ki stays small at 0.05 to avoid windup. base_speed is reduced from 1.2 to 1.0 because the baseline already left the line at 1.2 and the new geometry is untested; the time budget is a risk I accept, and the next race will show whether completion_time is limited by speed. line_loss stays last_direction, which re-enters the line on the side it was lost from. Expected result, as a hypothesis to test: fewer line-loss events than the 1.0 to 1.55 seen in iteration 0, and max_error below 0.06 m on at least one development track. Measurements requested cover the full set needed to answer the Builder's questions per track.
